note: PLAA is essential for mammalian development; complete null models in mice are embryonic/perinatal lethal, whereas reported human patients harbor hypomorphic variants causing postnatal neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

evidence.text: Hall et al. showed that PLAA is essential for mammalian embryonic development, and in both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures.

source.title: PLAA mutations cause a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy by disrupting ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation of synaptic proteins
source.quote: In both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures.

evidence.text: Falik Zaccai et al. identified a homozygous missense variant causing leukoencephalopathy and noted that complete Plaa-null mice were perinatal lethal.

source.title: Phospholipase A2-activating protein is associated with a novel form of leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: Plaa-null mice were perinatal lethal with reduced brain levels of prostaglandin E2
